## Body

Complements the existing returning-holder/queue-trigger note; its intermediate-state polling lesson need not be repeated.

#275 exposed two traps: list_panes prefers the control client but can fork tmux on fallback; list_panes_without_launch/query_live is the strict no-start/no-fork surface. A deadline checked only before sleep/read does not bound a blocking read. Offload synchronous work, await it against one deadline, and cap sleeps to the remaining budget; the fresh locked observation must still decide from its own evidence, never interpret an abandoned read as absence.

Abandoning a blocking JoinHandle does not cancel its job. There is at most one unfinished job per helper invocation, not per seat; concurrent/repeated invocations can accumulate them. The control client's three-second REPLY_TIMEOUT bounds reply reception only, not mutex acquisition, pipe writes or child reaping. Detached reads cannot alter seat authority/registry, but may finish existing control cleanup. Keep request-wait and whole-worker-lifetime claims separate (R275-FU-01).

Measure the handler interval separately from total testcase time: runtime teardown can wait for abandoned work after the response. Tight unscaled wall-clock bounds and exact poll counts are scheduler-sensitive (R275-FU-02).

Proof: final #275 head 10c8debed4cd5a46080ca96fda669f8c69140298, verdict bfbf6878; independently caught launching-read M5 and unbounded-read M6, then restored source and passed all 23 revive tests. These follow-ups were notes under C34, not another review round.
